newsitem.title: MEXICO: OECD sees Mexican growth at five pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: OECD sees Mexican growth at five pct in 1997.

text.p: Mexico's economy is likely to grow five percent in 1997, but the frailty of the banking system in the wake of the 1994-1995 peso crisis could put the brakes on the recovery, the OECD said in a report on Thursday.

The 1997 growth projection, contained in the Paris-based Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development's semi-annual economic outlook, is well above the government's forecast of at least four percent growth next year.
"The main downside risk is related to the fragility of the banking system, which could be a drag on growth," the OECD said.
It said the level of past-due loans, that soared as interest rates shot up in 1995, had stabilized, but that many firms and households continued to have payment problems.

Also, financial market stability and interest rates were "key factors in the unravelling of difficulties," it said. "Should market confidence continue to improve as assumed in the projection, possibilities of stronger growth cannot be excluded either."
